subset.rationale: immer's persistent containers bound head-on, four real concrete specializations listed explicitly (a spec's own template args are not signature-reachable): immer::vector<int>, immer::vector<std::string>, immer::map<int,int>, immer::set<int>. The differential's heart is value semantics with structural sharing: push_back/set/insert/erase RETURN A NEW container by value leaving the receiver untouched -- the test drives a chain of persistent updates through both native and Python and compares the CONTENTS OF EVERY intermediate version, asserting the original is unchanged after each op (12 differential + invariant tests, all green). Surfaces checked: size/empty/operator[]/at/back/front/push_back/set/take + value __eq__ on vector; size/count/operator[]/at/find/insert(pair)/set/erase on map; size/count/find/insert/erase on set; at() out-of-range/key-not-found error paths -> IndexError. The default_memory_policy + bits template machinery and the whole immer::detail implementation namespace (rbtree/champ/node/iterator) are reached only through internal members and are excluded via nb::exclude_ (see skipped_features).
skipped_features: the entire immer::detail namespace (rbts::rbtree/node/rbtree_iterator, hamts::champ/node/champ_iterator) excluded via nb::exclude_<^^immer::detail>. It is reachable from the public containers' begin()/end()/impl() but reflecting into it diverges HARD: the iterators derive from immer::detail::iterator_facade whose operator overloads re-check enable_if default template args naming its PROTECTED is_random_access/is_bidirectional from a no-access context (compile error), and the internal node types expose static factories whose pointer signatures trip the binder's static-method lambda. None of it is part of the persistent-value differential.

iterators (begin/end and the rbts/hamts iterator types) -- not bound; immer is a value-semantics library and the differential reads vectors out via size()/operator[], maps/sets via count/find. Excluded as part of immer::detail above.

the 2-argument fill constructor vector(size_type n, T v={}) of each vector spec -- excluded per-member via nb::exclude_. The binder emits nb::init<size_t,T> and nanobind's init<>::execute brace-inits Type{args...}, which a class also carrying an initializer_list<T> ctor (immer::vector does) hijacks toward that list: a hard narrowing error for vector<int>. See findings_draft/binder-init-braces-prefer-initializer-list.md. Not needed for the differential (vectors built persistently from empty()).

transient/mutable APIs (transient(), vector_transient/map_transient/set_transient) -- immer's escape hatch for batched in-place mutation; out of scope for the persistent-value differential, and transient() returns a detail-namespace-adjacent type. Not bound.
the std::initializer_list<T> constructors bind but are not Python-callable (no caster for initializer_list); harmless, never invoked.
update(key, Fn) / update(idx, Fn) -- take a function callback (member function template / non-defaulted Fn&&), gracefully skipped by the binder; persistent update is exercised via set() instead.
